articles.headline: Union cabinet approves ₹14,500 crore viability gap funding for energy storage
articles.summary: The Union cabinet approved ₹14,500 crore in viability gap funding to build 92GWh of grid-scale energy storage by FY31. The scheme supports battery energy storage and pumped storage projects estimated to cost ₹97,600 crore. Developers must source at least 40% of components from Indian manufacturers to ensure a reliable power supply and stabilize the electricity grid.

articles.headline: FAO Food Price Index rises 6% led by surging sugar prices
articles.summary: The FAO Food Price Index reached 115.4 in October, a 6% year-on-year increase. The surge was primarily driven by a 29% jump in sugar prices following concerns over India’s output due to deficient and uneven monsoon rainfall. Vegetable oil and dairy prices also saw significant increases, while meat and cereal indices remained relatively stable compared to the previous year.

articles.headline: Air pollution in Delhi and 200 cities skyrockets after Diwali festivities
articles.summary: Air quality deteriorated sharply across northern and central India after Diwali, with PM2.5 levels in Delhi reaching 500-700 micrograms per cubic metre—equivalent to smoking 25 cigarettes a day. While firecrackers caused a massive spike, stubble burning had already contributed up to 16.3% of the pollution load. Cold winter air is expected to trap pollutants until February.

articles.headline: Depleting reservoirs threaten India's rabi crops and hydropower generation
articles.summary: Water levels in 178 key Indian reservoirs are 27% lower than last year due to the weakest monsoon in decades. Storage in the southern region has plunged to 42.6% of capacity. The scarcity threatens irrigation for rabi crops like wheat and pulses and is expected to reduce hydropower generation, prompting the RBI to warn of mounting risks to food inflation.

articles.headline: JSW Group skips latest airport privatization round citing viability concerns
articles.summary: Billionaire Sajjan Jindal’s JSW Group has decided not to bid for the government’s latest bundle of 11 smaller airports, including Amritsar and Varanasi. An internal review concluded that the smaller assets are currently not profitable and resemble real estate investments rather than core infrastructure. The group may reconsider if major hubs like Kolkata or Chennai are auctioned.

articles.headline: Mid-size IT firms shift to commission-based incentives to lure sales talent
articles.summary: IT services firms like Hexaware and LTM are replacing quota-based sales targets with direct revenue-linked commissions to drive growth in the AI era. Hexaware has removed performance thresholds to let hunters get 'really rich' from new deals. LTM is specifically incentivizing 'AI-native' contracts, while Coforge is increasingly using external deal advisors to access opportunities.

articles.headline: Foreign regulatory data requests put Indian companies in legal bind
articles.summary: Indian firms are facing a surge in data requests from overseas regulators in the US, UK, and EU, creating conflicts with domestic laws. Companies in the IT, financial, and pharma sectors are seeking early legal advice to navigate confidentiality mandates and the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act. Failure to comply could have consequences under foreign jurisdictions.

articles.headline: Indian two-wheeler makers pivot to Latin America as Africa exports slide
articles.summary: Colombia has emerged as the top destination for Indian motorcycles as demand in Africa weakens. Exports to Colombia and Mexico rose over 80% since FY22, while Brazil saw a 706% surge. Bajaj, Hero, and TVS are investing in local manufacturing plants in the region to meet growing demand for delivery and courier vehicles amid a shift away from petrol bikes in traditional African markets.

articles.headline: Senate Democrats launch aggressive investigations into major American corporations
articles.summary: Following election victories, Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal has issued document-preservation requests to companies including Amazon, Apple, and Google. The probes target corporate ties to President Trump’s projects and alleged corruption. Companies are hiring specialized legal counsel to manage exposure to subpoenas and potential public hearings starting in January.

articles.headline: Manufacturers seek lower import duties to combat rising production costs
articles.summary: Industry bodies are urging the finance ministry to reduce basic customs duties on primary aluminium, graphite electrodes, and steel scrap in the 2027-28 budget. They argue high input costs make Indian goods less competitive. The Aluminium Extrusion Manufacturers Association noted that high raw material costs have led to the closure of 20 factories and the loss of 50,000 jobs.

articles.headline: Brent crude price drop to $90 offers relief to Indian economy
articles.summary: Brent crude fell below $90 a barrel for the first time since August, providing potential relief for India's fiscal deficit and state-run oil marketing companies. Lower prices could moderate inflation, reduce freight rates, and strengthen the rupee. However, experts warn that prices remain significantly higher than pre-war levels, maintaining pressure on government subsidies.

articles.headline: Government mandates electric vehicles as default choice for staff cars
articles.summary: The department of expenditure has directed all ministries to procure electric vehicles when replacing retired staff cars. The move aims to cut oil imports and vehicle emissions as India targets net-zero by 2070. The procurement ceiling for EVs has been set at ₹20 lakh, double the limit for internal combustion engine vehicles, signaling a major shift in official fleet policy.

articles.headline: Government identifies rainfed areas to expand domestic chana cultivation
articles.summary: The department of consumer affairs has identified 80 districts across states like Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan to increase chana (gram) production. By utilizing residual soil moisture in rainfed areas, the government aims to reduce import dependence and stabilize food prices. Chana imports fell to $3.63 billion in FY26, and the expansion could eventually create a surplus for export.

articles.headline: Draft rules propose certification for 900,000 allied health workers
articles.summary: The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions has released draft regulations requiring nearly 900,000 technicians to complete bridge courses and pass exams to retain their right to practice. The move aims to formalize qualifications for medical lab technicians, radiographers, and physiotherapists, who currently make up 60% of India's healthcare workforce.

articles.headline: India and US continue negotiations to finalize first trade deal tranche
articles.summary: Indian and US officials met in New Delhi to discuss customs and trade facilitation as part of an ongoing effort to finalize the first tranche of a proposed trade agreement. The talks represent continued engagement between the two nations following high-level diplomatic visits, focusing on reducing procedural barriers to bilateral commerce.

articles.headline: India's wheat planting hits record high amid weather concerns
articles.summary: Wheat planting in India is expected to reach record levels this season, though final output remains dependent on weather conditions through April 2027. The UN Food and Agriculture Organization noted that El Niño patterns could influence the harvest. Farmers are increasing acreage despite concerns over depleting reservoir levels in several key agricultural states.

articles.headline: Tata Steel domestic business drives 18% Ebitda growth in Q2
articles.summary: Tata Steel reported a consolidated Ebitda of ₹10,500 crore for the September quarter, an 18% year-on-year increase supported by domestic volumes. Standalone Ebitda grew 23% to ₹10,315 crore. However, overseas operations in the UK and Netherlands remained in losses due to lower sales volumes and environmental compliance shutdowns, despite higher realizations.

articles.headline: Axis Bank develops AI assistant to increase digital loan conversions
articles.summary: Axis Bank is building an AI-powered assistant to guide customers through online personal loan applications. Currently, only 8 out of 100 applicants complete the digital process; the bank aims to raise this to 12-15% using interactive AI. The initiative follows a push that saw digital originations reach 84% of personal loan payouts in the September quarter.

articles.headline: LG Electronics India reports 20% revenue growth in Q2FY27
articles.summary: LG Electronics India’s revenue grew nearly 20% to ₹7,380 crore in the September quarter, driven by premiumization in home appliances and air solutions. Ebitda margins expanded to 9.5% despite higher commodity costs. The company is now focusing on B2B opportunities in vehicle solutions and information displays to sustain double-digit growth.

articles.headline: Retail investors prune portfolios, concentrating on blue-chip stocks
articles.summary: Retail ownership declined in nearly half of BSE-listed companies in the September quarter as small investors became more selective. Despite the trend, Reliance Industries and HDFC Bank added over a million new retail shareholders. Analysts interpret the data as portfolio 'clean-up' rather than a loss of faith, with investors moving into established businesses with better valuations.

articles.headline: Indian sugar mills face margin squeeze due to ethanol restrictions
articles.summary: Operating margins for sugar mills are expected to contract by 140-160 basis points this fiscal. The decline is attributed to government restrictions on using sugar-based feedstocks for ethanol production, combined with rising sugarcane costs and stagnant ethanol prices. Profits from C-heavy molasses are insufficient to offset the loss of higher-margin ethanol output.

articles.headline: FMCG firms face volume-margin stress amid rising crude and rural woes
articles.summary: India's top consumer goods companies are struggling with rising input costs and uneven demand. Market leader HUL prioritized volume growth over margins, while Tata Consumer raised prices for salt and tea to offset costs. Analysts warn that high crude prices and low reservoir levels for rabi sowing could weigh on rural consumption in the second half of the fiscal year.

articles.headline: India Inc turns to non-permanent workers to manage cost pressures
articles.summary: Non-permanent employees, including contract and fixed-term workers, accounted for 17% of the workforce at 353 BSE 500 companies in FY26, up from 11% in FY23. Volatile demand and high crude-linked operating costs are prompting firms to seek flexible staffing. While this offers cost benefits, experts warn it may lead to a loss of institutional knowledge and skills.

articles.headline: Muthoot Microfin increases IT spending by 40% to combat cyberattacks
articles.summary: Muthoot Microfin Ltd has raised its IT budget by 40% this year to strengthen cybersecurity and digital infrastructure against AI-assisted attacks. The firm is focusing on securing its in-house app, used by 2.2 million customers. The move comes amid government warnings of escalating cyber threats targeting Indian financial institutions.

articles.headline: Renewable platform Resolven closes $900 million in total financing
articles.summary: EQT-backed Resolven has mobilized approximately $900 million in financing since becoming an independent entity in February. This includes a recent $219.5 million package for 400MW of wind-solar hybrid projects. The funding, sourced from 15 global and domestic lenders, consists of $700 million in debt and $200 million in non-fund lines.

articles.headline: Microsoft urges Trump administration to stop ban on Chinese data hardware
articles.summary: Microsoft is lobbying the Trump administration to halt a planned ban on Chinese optical transceivers, critical components for AI data centres. The US government cites national security concerns, fearing the parts could be used by Beijing for data theft or malware. Microsoft argues the ban could disrupt essential services and slow the growth of US data infrastructure.

articles.headline: TSMC approves $1 billion investment in Anthropic and OpenAI
articles.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) will invest up to $500 million in Anthropic’s common shares during its IPO and another $500 million in OpenAI’s preferred stock. The move deepens ties between the world’s leading chipmaker and the two most prominent frontier AI labs as they seek to secure massive computing power for future model development.

articles.headline: Dun & Bradstreet survey shows Indian businesses increasing AI spending
articles.summary: A survey of over 10,000 global firms found that 70% of Indian businesses plan to increase AI spending in the next 12 months. However, only 3% described their data as 'fully ready' for AI scale, compared to 8% globally. A significant talent gap remains, with only 25% of Indian firms reporting strong workforce readiness to utilize the new technology effectively.

articles.headline: ASK Investment Managers acquires Pune-based SageOne Investment Managers
articles.summary: ASK Investment Managers is acquiring SageOne, merging two houses to manage a combined ₹22,500 crore in assets. SageOne founder Samit Vartak will become CIO of the combined entity, overseeing 16 schemes. The deal provides SageOne with ASK’s massive distribution network while helping ASK address recent underperformance in its portfolio management services.

articles.headline: Investor Mukul Agrawal buys Worli office space for ₹163 crore
articles.summary: Veteran investor Mukul Agrawal has purchased 20,000 square feet of office space in an under-construction Lodha Developers project in Mumbai's Worli for ₹163.08 crore. The transaction, registered through Param Capital, covers the entire 46th floor. The deal reflects continued high demand for premium commercial real estate in Mumbai’s upscale business districts.

articles.headline: Digital-first beauty brands expand offline to reach neighbourhood shoppers
articles.summary: Brands like Honasa (Mamaearth), Nykaa, and Plum are aggressively expanding their physical retail presence. Since online channels only account for 25% of beauty sales in India, these companies are targeting general and modern trade outlets. Honasa reported 40% growth in general trade sales, while Nykaa's beauty arm saw 20% like-for-like growth across 338 outlets.

articles.headline: Forevermark targets 100 India stores and $100 million revenue
articles.summary: De Beers-owned Forevermark plans to expand its Indian retail footprint to 100 stores over five years. The strategy involves moving from partner jewellers to owned and franchised outlets to control design and experience. The brand plans to open stores in 20 cities, including metros and tier-2 markets like Guwahati and Ranchi, to tap into India's growing luxury diamond market.

articles.headline: IndiGo opposes GMR’s proposed distance-based user fees at Bhogapuram airport
articles.summary: GMR Airports has proposed doubling user development fees (UDF) at the upcoming Bhogapuram airport and introducing India’s first distance-based domestic fee structure. IndiGo has formally objected, arguing that higher charges will hurt passenger demand in a price-sensitive market. GMR claims the fees are essential to recover the ₹5,640 crore infrastructure investment.

articles.headline: Bollywood adapts remake strategy as streaming availability kills discovery value
articles.summary: Hindi cinema is pivoting away from frame-by-frame remakes of regional hits because originals are now widely available with subtitles on streaming platforms. Recent failures of films like 'Vikram Vedha' have prompted producers to seek proven intellectual property but create fresh theatrical narratives, as seen with 'Drishyam 3', which will differ significantly from its Malayalam original.

articles.headline: India flags developed nations' climate finance obligations at COP31
articles.summary: At the COP31 summit in Türkiye, India reiterated that developed nations must honor their commitments to provide financial resources for climate action in poorer countries. India stressed the principle of 'Common But Differentiated Responsibilities', arguing that the Global South cannot shoulder rising climate costs while still meeting basic development needs.

articles.headline: US-led trilateral peace talks for Russia and Ukraine begin in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are leading a new round of peace negotiations between Russian and Ukrainian officials in Abu Dhabi. The talks focus on ceasefire monitoring, de-escalation measures, and post-war security guarantees. This represents a significant effort by the Trump administration to restart the diplomatic process after months of stalled progress.

articles.headline: China’s trade surplus reaches record $1 trillion amid export surge
articles.summary: China’s trade surplus hit $1.04 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, driven by massive exports of electric vehicles, semiconductors, and industrial robots. Exports rose 35% in October alone. The deluge has sparked alarm in Europe and the US over industrial hollowing, as Chinese firms move production overseas to find customers amid a weak domestic economy.

articles.headline: Travellers swap flights for road trips as domestic airfares surge 40%
articles.summary: Soaring aviation fuel costs and weak currency have pushed domestic airfares up 30-40% year-on-year, prompting Indian holidaymakers to change year-end plans. Many are opting for long-distance road trips or train travel to avoid paying nearly ₹30,000 for a single domestic ticket. Some groups have swapped international destinations like Vietnam for domestic luxury stays in Kerala.

articles.headline: Xiaomi Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 proves effective during Delhi smog
articles.summary: Xiaomi’s new Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 (₹17,999) successfully reduced indoor AQI to 50 during Delhi’s peak pollution day where outdoor levels hit 1500. The device covers up to 940sqft and features a High-Efficiency Filter with UV light to prevent bacterial growth. The integrated RFID tag prevents the use of aftermarket filters, ensuring long-term maintenance of original standards.

articles.headline: Only Two Applications Received in Second Round of Coal Gasification Scheme
articles.summary: The government’s ₹37,500 crore scheme to promote coal and lignite gasification received only two applications in its second round, both from state-run NTPC. Experts cite difficulties in securing financing, uncertainty over coal supply, and a lack of assured buyers for products as primary factors hindering private investment. The third round has been opened with a deadline of January 11, 2027.

articles.headline: Government Targets ₹6,000 Crore From Sale of MTNL Land Assets
articles.summary: The Centre is considering monetising non-core assets worth up to ₹6,000 crore owned by debt-laden MTNL to repay liabilities. Five properties in Mumbai, valued at ₹4,000 crore, have received preliminary approval for sale. MTNL's liabilities rose to ₹40,000 crore in FY26, and the company has defaulted on loan repayments to several major public sector banks, including State Bank of India.

articles.headline: State-Owned Oil Companies Report Profit Bonanza Despite Global Crude Turmoil
articles.summary: State-owned oil marketing companies (OMCs) reported a 66.2% year-on-year jump in combined net profit to ₹29,896.1 crore for Q2FY27. Improved refining margins and a significant reduction in excise duty payouts offset losses from retail fuel sales. The companies benefited from not passing on a March excise duty cut to consumers, which expanded their marketing margins.

articles.headline: Foreign Investors Return to Indian Markets with ₹54,000 Crore Inflow
articles.summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have poured nearly ₹54,000 crore into Indian equities in early November, reversing a 10-month selloff. The shift is accompanied by increased buying of government securities via the Fully Accessible Route. Easing crude oil prices and the results of the US midterm elections have prompted a reassessment of exposure to Indian assets.

articles.headline: Centre Doubles Open Market Rice Sales Target to 5 Million Tonnes
articles.summary: To cool domestic prices and increase supplies, the government has doubled its open market rice sale target to 5 million tonnes for FY27. This comes amid production concerns in southern states due to low rainfall. The Centre has also made it mandatory for traders to disclose rice and paddy stocks every Friday and allowed several states to impose stock limits until January 2027.

articles.headline: Storm Clouds Gather Over COP31 Climate Finance and Trade Talks
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, opened with significant friction between developed and developing nations over climate finance and trade. Developing countries are pushing for established nations to meet an annual finance target of $300 billion by 2035. The UN warns that fossil fuel dependence continues to drive the crisis, while 2026 is on track to be the warmest year on record.

articles.headline: Intercity Bus Travel Gains Momentum Amid Soaring Domestic Airfares
articles.summary: India's intercity bus market is seeing strong growth as airfares rise by 20–40% and train tickets remain difficult to secure. Platforms like AbhiBus and EaseMyTrip report significant booking increases on leisure and pilgrimage routes. For journeys between 200–500 kilometres, travellers are increasingly choosing high-quality sleeper buses as a practical and cost-effective alternative.

articles.headline: Gold Smuggling Jumps 16-Fold Following Customs Duty Increase
articles.summary: Gold smuggling into India rose to 50 tonnes in the July-September quarter, accounting for 37% of total supply. The surge followed the government's decision to hike import duty from 6% to 15%. The domestic market discount of $43 an ounce signals active illicit channels, leading jewellers to call for a review of the duty to curb the appeal of the grey market.

articles.headline: Wall Street Falls as Hot Inflation Data Fuels Interest Rate Fears
articles.summary: Major US indices slipped after October inflation data came in higher than expected, suggesting the Federal Reserve may keep interest rates elevated. Shares of Nvidia dropped 4.4% amid reports of an FBI investigation. Brent crude prices briefly fell below $90 per barrel as investors weighed the possibility of peace talks between the US and Iran.

articles.headline: Leading Mutual Fund Commission Payouts Surge 12 Per Cent in FY26
articles.summary: The ten largest mutual fund houses paid ₹16,551 crore in commissions in FY26, up 12% year-on-year. SBI Mutual Fund recorded the highest payout at ₹3,159 crore. While overall payouts rose, commissions to sponsor banks grew at a slower rate of 9%, as AMCs increasingly diversified their distributor mix. Direct plans continue to gain popularity among retail investors.

articles.headline: CCI Clears Advent International’s ₹3,150 Crore Investment in Yatharth Hospital
articles.summary: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved a ₹3,150 crore primary capital infusion by US private equity firm Advent International into Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services. The deal allows Advent to acquire a 24.9% stake. Yatharth plans to use the funds to expand its capacity from 2,800 beds to over 5,000 beds within the next three years.

articles.headline: Dabur India Hints at Price Hikes to Counter Rising Input Costs
articles.summary: FMCG major Dabur India is considering calibrated price increases across its product portfolio to offset inflation in raw material costs. Rising crude oil prices due to the West Asia conflict have pressured supply chain margins. The company aims to sustain growth through cost optimisation and an improved product mix while navigating a challenging inflationary environment.

articles.headline: International Air Passenger Traffic in India Reaches 78.7 Million
articles.summary: India's international air passenger traffic grew by over 6% to reach 78.7 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026. However, the share of Indian carriers in overseas traffic declined to 44.4%. Data from the DGCA shows that 2,218 aircraft were registered in the country as of March 31, with 985 planes belonging to scheduled airlines.

articles.headline: Non-Metro Urban Markets Drive Over Half of Incremental Car Sales
articles.summary: Smaller cities and towns accounted for 55% of the growth in India's passenger vehicle registrations between January and October. While rural India saw the fastest growth rate at 27%, non-metro urban markets added the highest absolute number of vehicles (389,401). Metros, by contrast, recorded more mature, slower growth as demand shifted toward replacement purchases.

articles.headline: CNH to Make India Leadership Base for Global Software Operations
articles.summary: Global equipment manufacturer CNH is consolidating its technology teams, making India the leadership base for its global software operations. The company's India Global Capability Centre will now build and run technology used across five global regions. CNH aims to double its global in-house IT headcount in India by 2028 while heavily integrating AI tools into operations.

articles.headline: Aftermarket Chain myTVS to Enter West Asian Market by 2027
articles.summary: Multi-brand car service chain myTVS plans to expand into West Asia by April 2027, partnering with UAE-based Crescent Enterprises. The company recently raised ₹425 crore in funding to support domestic growth and global expansion. myTVS expects to cross ₹2,000 crore in revenue this financial year and aims to double that figure over the next three years.

articles.headline: Adani Power Fast-Tracks ₹30,000 Crore Thermal Power Project in Odisha
articles.summary: Adani Power has moved its proposed 2,400 MW ultra-supercritical thermal power project in Odisha into the environmental clearance stage. The ₹30,181 crore project is expected to consume 9.67 million tonnes of coal annually and draw water from the Mahanadi river. A public hearing is scheduled for December 18 as the company moves toward final regulatory approvals.

articles.headline: Smartphone Volumes Slump 20 Per Cent This Diwali Amid Price Hikes
articles.summary: India's smartphone market saw an 18–20% drop in volume sales during the Diwali season compared to last year. While premium phone demand spiked during Dhanteras, it failed to offset a sharp pre-festival slump. Higher global memory chip rates pushed up prices, causing many budget-conscious buyers to either delay purchases or opt for pre-owned devices.

articles.headline: India and US Agree on Coordinated Action Against Drug Threats
articles.summary: During a high-level meeting in New Delhi, India and the US agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation to address emerging narcotic threats. Priority areas include intelligence sharing, pharmaceutical supply chain integrity, and drug demand reduction. The meeting was part of the India-US Drug Policy Executive Working Group aimed at combatting illicit drug trafficking.

articles.headline: Karnataka Farmers to Receive Minimum ₹5,000 in Drought Relief Assistance
articles.summary: Deputy CM G Parameshwara clarified that every eligible drought-affected farmer in Karnataka will receive a minimum of ₹5,000. Farmers who received smaller initial amounts will be paid the balance in subsequent instalments. The state government has authorized the release of ₹2,500 per eligible farmer as the first part of the input subsidy relief package.

articles.headline: Social Activist and Barefoot College Founder Sanjit Bunker Roy Dies
articles.summary: Renowned social activist Sanjit Bunker Roy, founder of Barefoot College, passed away at the age of 81 in Ajmer, Rajasthan. Roy spent over five decades working to empower rural communities and women through self-reliance and education. His work turned the village of Tilonia into a globally recognized centre for rural development and grassroots empowerment.

articles.headline: Compliance Concessions Drive 80 Per Cent Surge in Company Strike-Offs
articles.summary: Over 21,800 companies were struck off the government register between April and October, an 80% increase year-on-year. A Ministry of Corporate Affairs scheme offering steep fee reductions encouraged thousands of inactive businesses to formally exit. Most were small private firms and startups that had accumulated years of pending annual filings and statutory defaults.

articles.headline: Parliamentary Panel Omit Air Pollution Discussion From Upcoming Meeting Agenda
articles.summary: The Parliamentary Committee on Home Affairs has dropped the issue of NCR air pollution from its November 17 meeting agenda, sparking objections from Congress members. Despite the worsening air quality in Delhi, the topic was removed in a revised agenda. The move has led to criticism regarding the panel's focus on urgent public health and environmental crises.

articles.headline: PHDCCI Proposes Eliminating Basic Customs Duty on LNG and Naphtha
articles.summary: The PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry has recommended removing basic Customs duty on liquefied natural gas, naphtha, and heavy petroleum feedstocks in the upcoming Budget. The industry body argues these measures are essential to lower manufacturing costs and improve India's global competitiveness. It also sought the continuation of the current duty framework on steel scrap.

articles.headline: Climate Change May Push 141 Million More Women Into Extreme Poverty
articles.summary: A UN fact sheet reports that climate change could push up to 141 million additional women and girls into extreme poverty by 2050 under worst-case scenarios. Temperature rises are associated with women losing 34% more income than men. The report calls for a 'gender-just' transition to deliver job gains for women and address the widening gender gap in food insecurity.

articles.headline: PhysicsWallah to Invest ₹200 Crore for Online Business Acquisitions
articles.summary: Edtech firm PhysicsWallah plans to acquire two to three online companies this year with a budget of ₹200 crore. The acquisitions will focus on expanding capabilities in artificial intelligence and entering new examination categories. Cofounder Prateek Maheshwari noted that the firm's online segment grew 29.3% in the first half of FY27, prompting deeper investment in South India.

articles.headline: Amazon to Deploy AI Agents to Help 15 Million Small Businesses
articles.summary: Amazon India plans to bring AI-powered tools to 15 million small businesses by 2030 to identify opportunities and act on their behalf. The company reported that over 70% of businesses in its recent festival sale came from Tier-II and Tier-III cities. To encourage growth, Amazon has reduced seller fees for products priced below ₹1,000 and simplified the listing process using AI.

articles.headline: Qantas to Cut 850 Jobs and Offshore Functions to Accenture
articles.summary: Australian airline Qantas will cut 850 corporate jobs and outsource functions to Accenture in response to the increased use of AI. The cuts, affecting 3% of its workforce, will impact finance, procurement, and marketing roles. Many of the outsourced roles will be shifted to teams based in India. Qantas cited the need to overhaul legacy systems and access global AI talent.

articles.headline: India Offers a Compelling Opportunity for AI Investment Says Mahindra
articles.summary: Mahindra Group Chairman Anand Mahindra stated that India’s software talent and domestic market create a unique AI opportunity that goes beyond chip manufacturing. He argued that the real growth lies in AI applications and enterprise-wide deployment. Mahindra suggested that the renewed interest from global investors in Indian equities may have more staying power than previously thought.

articles.headline: Cognizant Commit 25,000 Professionals to Claude AI Delivery Group
articles.summary: Cognizant has formed the Claude Frontier Capability Group, dedicating over 25,000 professionals to delivering Anthropic’s Claude AI for clients. The initiative includes a managed services model to take AI pilots into enterprise-scale production. The group will focus on developing certified engineers to help businesses overcome challenges in realizing actual value from frontier AI models.

articles.headline: Medical Device PLI Scheme Extended to 2036 with ₹2,700 Crore Outlay
articles.summary: The Department of Pharmaceuticals has extended the medical device production-linked incentive scheme by eight years. The revised framework relaxes eligibility conditions, reducing minimum investment requirements and extending timelines for setting up facilities. The focus will shift toward promoting domestic manufacturing of high-end medical consumables, implants, and critical components.

articles.headline: Analysis Shows Firecracker Mishaps Occur Year-Round at Manufacturing Units
articles.summary: NCRB data reveals that firework-related accidents in India are not limited to the Diwali period, with many casualties occurring at manufacturing hubs like Sivakasi throughout the year. In 2026, major incidents at nine factories, mostly illegal, claimed 92 lives. Adults aged 18–44 are the primary victims, accounting for over 60% of all firecracker-related deaths since 2015.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh Achieves 74 Per Cent Conversion Rate on Investment Proposals
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh has successfully converted 526 out of 714 investment projects received since June 2024 into active projects. These represent investments worth ₹17.2 trillion with a potential for 1.93 million jobs. The state is preparing to host the 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, which is expected to draw representatives from 58 countries and global investors.

articles.headline: India Engages Russia and Ukraine to Establish Safe Black Sea Shipping
articles.summary: India is negotiating with both Russia and Ukraine to guarantee the safety of shipping in the Black Sea for grain and energy exports. The MEA has exchange ideas on creating 'food corridors' to protect Global South interests from the impact of El Niño. Meanwhile, the ministry dismissed as 'malicious' legal allegations made by a separatist leader in a US court against Indian officials.

articles.headline: Tea Board Recommends Minimum Sustainable Price to Support Indian Estates
articles.summary: A Tea Board of India committee has proposed introducing a Minimum Sustainable Price (MSP) for tea to address the gap between production costs and market prices. Industry bodies welcomed the move, noting that labor costs account for 60% of total production expenses. The MSP would be determined by a composite index reflecting wage movements and the consumer price index.

articles.headline: Editorial: India Must Prepare for AI-Led Global Investment Volatility
articles.summary: US midterm election results favoring Democrats could slow AI development and data centre construction due to environmental and resource concerns. Such a policy shift in the US might drive AI investments toward India. However, India must adopt clear water and power usage policies for data centres to handle the pressure and prepare for potential financial market volatility as AI trades unwind.

articles.headline: Opinion: India Needs New Policy Approach Beyond 1991 Delicensing
articles.summary: Nitin Desai argues that while the 1991 delicensing shifted investment from the public to the private sector, it has not significantly accelerated manufacturing growth. Unlike China, India has struggled with technologically-led startups and exports. The reforms of the 1990s are no longer sufficient to address current challenges in agriculture, manufacturing, and lower-income employment.

articles.headline: Analysis: West Asia Crisis Poses Risk to India's Fiscal Deficit Target
articles.summary: Aditi Nayar writes that the West Asia crisis and elevated crude oil prices are straining India's fiscal health through higher subsidies and reduced tax revenues. Under-recoveries on LPG and higher fertilizer subsidy requirements could lead to a fiscal gap of 0.7% of GDP. However, strong small savings inflows and non-tax revenues from stake sales may limit actual fiscal slippage.

articles.headline: Individual Equity Ownership in NSE Firms Reaches Record 19.5 Per Cent
articles.summary: Combined equity ownership by individual investors in firms listed on the National Stock Exchange hit a record high of 19.5% in September. This includes direct holdings and indirect investments through mutual funds. In contrast, foreign portfolio investor ownership fell to a 21-year low of 14.7% as domestic households continued to increase their exposure to the stock market.

articles.headline: Attractive Valuations and Firm Oil Prices Support Gains in ONGC
articles.summary: ONGC reported Q2FY27 Ebitda of ₹26,300 crore, supported by high Brent crude prices. While production declined slightly due to technical disruptions, the company is fast-tracking deepwater exploration and offshore development. Analysts believe ONGC's current valuation remains attractive, offering a logical case for share appreciation despite ongoing concerns regarding production growth targets.

articles.headline: Apollo Hospitals Delivers Strong Q2 Performance Supported by Patient Volumes
articles.summary: Apollo Hospitals reported a 23% revenue growth in Q2FY27, led by inpatient volume increases and an improved case mix. The hospital chain is planning to add 6,000 beds over the next five years. Most brokerages remain positive on the stock, citing margin expansion in the pharmacy business and potential value unlocking in its digital healthcare platform, Apollo 24/7.

articles.headline: New Motor Insurance Norms to Allow Customised Coverage from December 15
articles.summary: Irdai is introducing a four-layer framework for motor insurance, allowing buyers to pick optional covers like occupant liability while keeping third-party liability mandatory. The new system mandates standard wording for policies to make them easier to compare. While this offers more choice, experts warn that dropping essential covers just to save on premiums could prove expensive during a claim.

articles.headline: Brokerages Bullish on Samvat 2083 Following November Equity Rally
articles.summary: A 9% rally in the Sensex during early November has restored investor optimism for the new Hindu year, Samvat 2083. Brokerages predict the index could gain nearly 14% over the next year, reaching 92,170. Top Diwali stock picks include Tata Steel, Mahindra & Mahindra, Hindalco, and Axis Bank, supported by expected double-digit earnings growth and continued FPI buying.

articles.headline: Lessons From the Binance Heist for India's Cryptocurrency Ecosystem
articles.summary: A $6.3 billion cyber-heist at Binance highlights the sophisticated techniques used by state-linked hacking groups against crypto exchanges. Experts note that attackers often target human vulnerabilities and trusted devices rather than breaking encryption. Indian exchanges are following a risk-based approach, focusing on wallet exposure management and layered access controls to prevent similar heists.

articles.headline: Delhi Launches First Yamuna Cruise Service Namo Yamuna River Safari
articles.summary: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal and Delhi CM Rekha Gupta flagged off the capital's first Yamuna cruise service. Named the Namo Yamuna River Safari, the 30-passenger vessel will operate on a 4–5 kilometre stretch between Sonia Vihar and Jagatpur. Each 40-minute ride aims to promote river tourism and awareness of the waterway's ecological health in the national capital.

articles.headline: PM: Govt working to make India self-reliant in defence
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that the government is committed to making India self-reliant in defence production. He highlighted efforts to boost domestic manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports, aiming for global competitiveness in the defence sector.

articles.headline: India-US hold talks on Indo-Pacific, defence, tech
articles.summary: India and the United States concluded strategic and commercial dialogues, covering the Indo-Pacific region, defence cooperation, and emerging technologies. Both nations reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and addressing shared global challenges.

articles.headline: EC likely to announce poll schedule for 5 states soon
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India is expected to announce the schedule for assembly elections in five states shortly. Preparations are in final stages, with the EC reviewing readiness and logistical arrangements for the upcoming electoral process.

articles.headline: Global economic growth forecast revised down by IMF
articles.summary: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has revised its global economic growth forecast downwards, citing persistent inflation, geopolitical tensions, and slowing growth in major economies. The revised projection signals a challenging outlook for the global economy.

articles.headline: SC to hear pleas against state budget approval
articles.summary: The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear petitions challenging the approval process of a state budget. The case involves significant legal questions regarding legislative procedures and financial oversight within state governance structures.

articles.headline: New study reveals impact of climate change on water resources
articles.summary: A recent scientific study has quantified the impact of climate change on freshwater resources, indicating significant shifts in precipitation patterns and increased water scarcity in several regions. The findings underscore the urgency of climate action.

articles.headline: India's infrastructure development focus: Roads and Railways
articles.summary: The Indian government is prioritizing infrastructure development, with a significant push on expanding road networks and modernizing railway infrastructure. Projects aim to improve connectivity, logistics efficiency, and national economic growth.

articles.headline: India's tech sector sees surge in AI adoption
articles.summary: India's technology sector is witnessing a rapid increase in the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions across various industries. Companies are leveraging AI for automation, data analysis, and enhanced customer experiences.

articles.headline: Major cities face water stress due to delayed monsoon
articles.summary: Several major Indian cities are experiencing water stress due to delayed monsoon rains. Water levels in reservoirs are declining, prompting authorities to implement water conservation measures and explore alternative supply options.

articles.headline: RBI warns of rising inflation risks
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has cautioned about persistent inflation risks, stating that elevated price levels could impact economic stability. The central bank indicated it would continue to monitor the situation and take appropriate monetary policy measures.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to expedite hearing on Article 370 case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has decided to expedite the hearing of petitions challenging the abrogation of Article 370 of the Constitution. The court aims to provide a swift resolution to the complex legal and constitutional matter.

articles.headline: India's trade deficit widens in the last quarter
articles.summary: India's trade deficit has widened in the last fiscal quarter, primarily due to an increase in imports exceeding export growth. Economic analysts are closely watching the trend for its potential impact on the country's balance of payments.

articles.headline: Health Ministry launches new public health campaign
articles.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has launched a new public health campaign focused on preventive healthcare and disease management. The initiative aims to raise awareness and promote healthier lifestyles among citizens.

articles.headline: Educational reforms proposed for skill development
articles.summary: The Ministry of Education has proposed significant reforms aimed at enhancing skill development and vocational training programs. The changes are designed to align educational outcomes with industry demands and improve employability.

articles.headline: India participates in global climate summit
articles.summary: India has actively participated in a global climate summit, reiterating its commitment to climate action and renewable energy targets. The country presented its progress and discussed collaborative strategies for mitigating climate change effects.

articles.headline: Cultural festival showcases diverse Indian arts
articles.summary: A national cultural festival is underway, celebrating the rich diversity of Indian art forms, music, and dance. The event aims to promote cultural exchange and preserve traditional artistic heritage across the nation.

articles.headline: New bridge project to boost regional connectivity
articles.summary: A new ambitious bridge project has been inaugurated, aimed at significantly boosting regional connectivity and easing transportation. The infrastructure development is expected to enhance economic activity in the surrounding areas.

articles.headline: Sports Ministry announces support for emerging athletes
articles.summary: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has announced enhanced support for emerging athletes, including financial aid and advanced training facilities. The initiative aims to nurture talent and improve India's performance in international sports.

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders status quo on land acquisition
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered a status quo on a controversial land acquisition case, pending further hearings. The decision impacts a significant development project and raises questions about land rights.

articles.headline: Scientists discover new species in Western Ghats
articles.summary: Researchers have announced the discovery of a new species of flora in the Western Ghats region. The finding highlights the region's biodiversity and the importance of conservation efforts.

articles.headline: Stock markets show mixed trends
articles.summary: Indian stock markets are exhibiting mixed trends, with key indices trading with minor fluctuations. Analysts attribute the performance to a combination of global economic cues and domestic corporate earnings reports.

articles.headline: Government reviews economic stimulus package
articles.summary: The government is reviewing the effectiveness of its existing economic stimulus package. Discussions are ongoing regarding potential adjustments or new measures to support key sectors and sustain economic recovery.

articles.headline: International trade agreement signed between India and bloc
articles.summary: India has signed a new international trade agreement with a regional economic bloc. The pact aims to boost trade volumes, reduce tariffs, and enhance economic cooperation between the parties.

articles.headline: New technology for water purification developed
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a novel technology for water purification, offering a more efficient and cost-effective solution for providing clean drinking water. The innovation has the potential to address water scarcity challenges.

articles.headline: India strengthens ties with African nations
articles.summary: India has reinforced its diplomatic and economic ties with several African nations through a series of high-level engagements. Discussions focused on trade, investment, and cooperation in areas like technology and infrastructure.

articles.headline: Cybersecurity threats on the rise, experts warn
articles.summary: Cybersecurity experts have warned of a significant rise in cybersecurity threats targeting individuals and organizations in India. They emphasize the need for enhanced security measures and public awareness campaigns.

articles.headline: National education policy implementation review
articles.summary: A comprehensive review of the implementation progress of the National Education Policy is underway. The government is assessing the effectiveness of reforms and identifying areas for further action.

articles.headline: India's space mission achieves key milestone
articles.summary: India's ambitious space mission has successfully achieved a critical milestone, marking significant progress in its scientific objectives. The achievement underscores India's growing capabilities in space exploration.

articles.headline: New agricultural techniques aim to boost crop yields
articles.summary: Innovative agricultural techniques are being introduced to enhance crop yields and improve farming practices across India. The focus is on sustainable agriculture and farmer prosperity.

articles.headline: World Health Organization issues dengue alert
articles.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued a global alert regarding a potential increase in dengue fever cases. Health authorities in India are strengthening surveillance and public awareness measures.

articles.headline: Major infrastructure project faces construction delays
articles.summary: A significant infrastructure project is experiencing construction delays, impacting its planned completion timeline. Authorities are investigating the reasons for the setbacks and working on mitigation strategies.

articles.headline: India secures new bilateral sports partnerships
articles.summary: India has established new bilateral sports partnerships with several countries to foster collaboration in athlete training and sports development. These agreements aim to enhance international sporting engagement.

articles.headline: New law proposed to regulate digital assets
articles.summary: The government is considering a new legal framework to regulate digital assets and cryptocurrencies. The proposed law aims to address concerns related to financial stability, consumer protection, and illicit activities.

articles.headline: India chairs international forum on sustainable development
articles.summary: India is chairing an international forum focused on sustainable development goals. The deliberations involve global leaders discussing strategies for achieving environmental protection and socio-economic progress.

articles.headline: Xiaomi Seeks Local Partners for White Goods Manufacturing in India
articles.summary: Xiaomi is scouting for local partners to manufacture white goods in India, following the launch of its Mijia sub-brand for home and lifestyle products. This strategic move, which starts on Page 1 and continues on Page 11, aims to diversify revenue, monetize its connected ecosystem, and strengthen its presence in India's consumer technology market.

articles.headline: US State Dept Serves Summons to NSA Doval, Ex-RAW Chief Goel
articles.summary: The US State Department served summons to NSA Ajit Doval and former RAW chief Samant Goel through diplomatic channels in a civil lawsuit filed by Sikhs for Justice's Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. India's MEA dismissed the lawsuit as "frivolous, fabricated and malicious." The lawsuit stems from a DoJ investigation into Nikhil Gupta, charged with conspiring to assassinate Pannun.

articles.headline: Ladakh Hill Development Council Polls Announced Amid Protests
articles.summary: The State Election Commission of Ladakh announced elections for all eight Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils for December 4, with results on December 8. This comes amid complete shutdowns and protests in Kargil and Sankoo demanding poll deferment and a delimitation review.

articles.headline: BJP Slams Sonia Gandhi's Memoir as 'Whitewashing' Historical Wrongs
articles.summary: BJP criticized Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging' as "whitewashing" historical wrongs, particularly for "justifying" the Emergency and giving a "clean chit" to Rajiv Gandhi on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots by blaming then-Army chief AS Vaidya, contrary to official records.

articles.headline: Ousted Bangladesh PM Hasina Must Face Death Sentence: Chief Prosecutor
articles.summary: Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that ousted PM Sheikh Hasina has no legal option but to face execution of her death sentence, rejecting passport issuance. Hasina intends to return in December to face legal proceedings.

articles.headline: Bengal Govt Announces Diwali Bonanza for IAS Officers
articles.summary: West Bengal government announced a Diwali bonanza for its IAS officers, including a 50% hike in sumptuary allowance (`60,000-`80,000/month), soft loans up to `50 lakh for children's higher education (India/abroad), expanded LTC to Southeast Asia/Dubai/Mauritius, and post-retirement benefits for apex-level retirees.

articles.headline: ED Probes Punjab CMO for Alleged ‘Parallel Power Centre’ Network
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate is investigating an alleged network of private intermediaries, including Nitin Gohal, operating around the Punjab Chief Minister’s Office (CMO). Allegations include influencing transfers, policy, tenders, and accessing confidential files, leading to a CBI FIR. The AAP government denies allegations.

articles.headline: TN CM Vijay Calls Emergency Meeting to Rein In TVK MLAs
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay called an emergency meeting of his TVK party legislators amid scrutiny over MLA conduct. This follows allegations against Deputy Speaker M Ravisankar for assault and Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh for sending obscene messages to a district collector.

articles.headline: India Proposes Three-Part Plan to De-escalate Ukraine War
articles.summary: India has presented Russia and Ukraine with a three-part framework to de-escalate the war, focusing on halting attacks on energy/critical infrastructure, ensuring Black Sea grain/energy shipments, and ending strikes on merchant vessels. PM Modi conveyed India's readiness for peaceful resolution.

articles.headline: Suvendu Adhikari Alleges Mamata Banerjee Hid Info in Poll Affidavit
articles.summary: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari alleged that former CM Mamata Banerjee concealed information in her affidavit for recent assembly elections, deeming it an "offence." Meanwhile, Delhi Police reportedly issued a fresh notice to Banerjee to record her statement as a 'victim' in a 2013 protest case.

articles.headline: Green Hydrogen Demand Slump Delays Electrolyser Plant Launches to Aug 2027
articles.summary: Lack of demand for green hydrogen forces companies like Reliance, Adani, and L&T to defer electrolyser manufacturing facility commissioning to August 2027 from December 2026. MNRE extended the deadline, allowing companies to retain PLI incentives, though without immediate financial benefit.

articles.headline: Maharashtra Transmission Company IPO Proposed for FY28
articles.summary: Maharashtra State Electricity Transmission Company (MSETCL) submitted an IPO proposal to the state government, targeting FY28 to raise `7,000-8,000 crore. Approval is expected soon, as the company seeks funds for tariff-based competitive bidding projects and expansion.

articles.headline: Carlos Prates, UFC's 'The Nightmare,' Set for Interim Welterweight Title Fight
articles.summary: UFC's No. 1 welterweight contender Carlos Prates, nicknamed 'The Nightmare,' will face Michael Morales for the interim championship on January 30, 2027. Prates, who has won all seven UFC fights by knockout, is pursuing the title after reigning champion Islam Makhachev declined a January bout.

articles.headline: Michael Carrick Expected to be Sacked as Manchester United Manager
articles.summary: Michael Carrick is reportedly set to be sacked as Manchester United manager following the team's dismal start to the season, their worst in 40 years. United is in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. Mauricio Pochettino is named as a top candidate.

articles.headline: India-New Zealand Third ODI Abandoned Due to Rain, India Retains 2-0 Lead
articles.summary: The third One-Day International between India and New Zealand in Hamilton was abandoned due to rain, with India retaining its 2-0 lead in the five-match series. The outcome ended New Zealand’s 11-consecutive home ODI series victory streak since 2019.

articles.headline: World Athletics Toughens Entry Standards for Los Angeles 2028 Olympics
articles.summary: World Athletics announced tougher entry standards for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, increasing reliance on world rankings. Approximately 40% of athletes will qualify via standards and 60% via rankings, a shift from the 50-50 split at Paris 2024.

articles.headline: Indian Shooters Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh Miss Olympic Quota
articles.summary: Indian shooters Manu Bhaker and Esha Singh failed to secure quota places for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics in the women's 25m pistol individual final at the ISSF World Championships in Doha. India settled for team gold.

articles.headline: Cricket Australia Rules Out Reopening 'Sandpapergate' Ball-Tampering Probe
articles.summary: Cricket Australia chief Todd Greenberg ruled out reopening the investigation into the 2018 'Sandpapergate' ball-tampering scandal, stating no "compelling reason" for a new probe. This follows Usman Khawaja's autobiography suggesting wider team knowledge of the plot.

articles.headline: 'Creamy Layer' Debate: Socioeconomic Advancement Beyond Income Alone
articles.summary: India's 'creamy layer' debate is re-examined, asserting that parental salary alone can't define status, requiring consideration of education, occupation, and assets. Data from 2004-23 shows significant economic convergence among SC, ST, and OBC households, but also growing differentiation within groups.

articles.headline: Govardhan Puja: Respect Nature and Humble Gratitude
articles.summary: Govardhan Puja, celebrated on the 4th day of Deepavali, commemorates Lord Krishna lifting the Govardhan Hill. It conveys a timeless message: respect nature, remain humble, and be grateful for life-sustaining resources, paralleling Wordsworth's philosophy of nature as a source of wisdom.

articles.headline: The Power of Sound: Understanding Brain's Processing of Auditory Environments
articles.summary: This podcast summary explores how our brains process sound, beyond simple hearing. Neurobiologist Nina Kraus explains sound processing as an active feedback loop shaped by memories. It emphasizes curating auditory environments to reduce urban noise stressors and strengthen neural connections.

articles.headline: US Midterm Elections Shift AI Policy Towards Scepticism and Regulation
articles.summary: Following the Republican defeat in US midterms, the new Democrat majority is seen as more "anti-AI," favoring regulation. This creates a collision course with Trump's pro-AI, less-regulated stance. AI safety-ists like Anthropic and OpenAI may find allies in Congress for stricter oversight.

articles.headline: E-rickshaws Crucial for Last-Mile Connectivity to Transport Hubs
articles.summary: L5 category electric 3-wheelers, e-rickshaws, and e-carts are vital for last-mile connectivity to metro stations and bus terminuses. With improved safety, policies, and test protocols, e-rickshaws can facilitate a significant shift from personal vehicles to public transport.

articles.headline: Vedant Fashions' Same-Store Sales Decline 5.8% Amid Competition
articles.summary: Vedant Fashions (Manyavar, Mohey) reported a 5.8% decline in same-store sales in Q2, with revenue up 2.4% and net profit flat. The company attributes weakness to festive calendar shifts and increased competition, acknowledging an urgent need to attract and increase purchases from new customers.

articles.headline: Ramayana Dominates Domestic Box Office, Global Push Falls Short
articles.summary: 'Ramayana: Part 1' earned nearly 60% of its `664-crore global haul from India, despite a 50,000-screen overseas release. Trade analysts note limited connect with Western audiences due to cultural relatability and lack of emotional depth in storytelling, challenging its global product positioning.

articles.headline: Honda to Build $3 Billion Hybrid Auto Plant in Ohio, Creating 2,000 Jobs
articles.summary: Honda Motor will invest $3 billion to build a new hybrid vehicle plant in Ohio, creating 2,000 jobs. The plant, operational by 2029, will produce 240,000 vehicles annually, increasing US capacity to 1.3 million. Honda is also investing in Canadian and other US operations.

articles.headline: Zara Owner Inditex Backs Fund to Cut Supply Chain Emissions
articles.summary: Inditex SA, owner of Zara, committed $50 million to a new fund led by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to provide low-cost loans to suppliers investing in energy efficiency. This aims to help the fashion industry reduce its 8% contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions.

articles.headline: Botswana to Double Stake in De Beers to 30%
articles.summary: Botswana's president announced the country will double its stake in De Beers to 30% under a proposed deal for a consortium to buy Anglo American’s shares. This move would make Botswana the largest single shareholder in the world's leading diamond company.

articles.headline: FDA Adds Eye-Risk Warning for Ozempic, Other GLP-1 Weight-Loss Drugs
articles.summary: The US FDA will add a warning about a rare eye condition, non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (vision loss due to decreased blood flow to optic nerve), to the labels of all GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, including Ozempic and Wegovy. The problem occurred in roughly 6 per 100,000 patients.

articles.headline: Air India Shortlists Former SIA Executive Balagopal Kunduvara for CFO
articles.summary: Air India has shortlisted Balagopal Kunduvara, former senior executive at Singapore Airlines and finance chief of Garuda Indonesia, for its Chief Financial Officer (CFO) position. This aims to strengthen financial management, rein in costs, and improve operational efficiency amid mounting losses.

articles.headline: Marvel Veteran Jeremy Latcham to Lead DC Studios as Co-CEOs Step Down
articles.summary: James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-CEOs of DC Studios after four years, following Skydance's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Jeremy Latcham, a Marvel Studios veteran, will take over as president and chief creative officer, effective December 1.

articles.headline: Prosus Intensifies India Fintech Investments, Eyes AI-led Credit Startup Oolka
articles.summary: Prosus plans to increase fintech investments in India, focusing on underserved customers and improving lending costs. It is close to investing in AI-led credit management startup Oolka and has invested over $8 billion in 30 Indian firms, with its India portfolio valued at $8 billion.

articles.headline: Quick Commerce Drives Record Festive Sales Growth for D2C Brands
articles.summary: Direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands saw strong festive sales growth, with many doubling last year's numbers, largely driven by quick commerce platforms. Consumers, though cautious, opted for higher-value products and concentrated purchases during promotional periods, boosting sales for gifting and essentials.

articles.headline: AI Giant Anthropic Unveils New Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 AI Models
articles.summary: AI giant Anthropic launched upgraded models—Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2—to advance coding, mathematics, cybersecurity, robotics, and scientific research. Mythos 5.2, with strong safeguards, offers advanced capabilities for vulnerability discovery and scientific research.

articles.headline: Lenskart, Meesho Deliver $400 Million Gains for SoftBank Vision Funds
articles.summary: SoftBank's Vision Funds realized nearly $400 million in gains from Lenskart ($273 million) and Meesho ($121 million) during Q3, making them top performers globally despite SoftBank's overall $7 billion net loss. SoftBank continues to monetize its Indian investments.

articles.headline: China Showcases Tech, AI Prowess at World Web Summit in Lisbon
articles.summary: China is leveraging the World Web Summit in Lisbon to display its technological prowess, featuring dancing robots and low-cost AI models. This comes amidst claims that Beijing spied on Nvidia and despite US export restrictions on advanced AI chips.

articles.headline: Moonshot AI Rents Nvidia's Top Chips in China Despite Export Curbs
articles.summary: Chinese AI champion Moonshot AI rented 3 Super Micro Computer servers equipped with Nvidia’s B300 GPUs this summer. This highlights its reliance on American hardware and Nvidia's continued market presence in China despite US export restrictions, as per Beijing regulatory filings.

articles.headline: Tata Electronics Directed to File Action Report After Gas Leak Deaths
articles.summary: Tata Electronics was directed by the Krishnagiri district collector to review safety and submit an action taken report after three contract workers died from asphyxiation at its effluent treatment plant. Industrial Safety and Health is conducting a detailed inspection.

articles.headline: Apple Intelligence Registered in China for iPad and Mac Use
articles.summary: Apple's generative AI service, Apple Intelligence, has been registered for use on iPads and Macs in China. This move follows China's requirement for companies to register large language models and generative AI services with regulators before public release.

articles.headline: Uber's Revenue Growth Faces Profitability Challenge Despite Bookings Surge
articles.summary: Uber's gross bookings and revenue continue to grow rapidly, reaching $59.8 billion and $14.8 billion respectively in Q3. However, despite these increases, the company recorded an operating income of $1.5 billion, indicating a potential hurdle in translating revenue growth into substantial profitability.

articles.headline: UK Banks Reduce AI Exposure Amid Market Correction Fears
articles.summary: UK banks are trimming their exposure to artificial intelligence due to concerns about a brutal correction in the sector, according to the Bank of England's top supervisor. Despite extensive interrogation, the BOE hasn't found evidence that lenders would amplify an AI shock.

articles.headline: Rippling Expands India AI Lab, Boosts Hiring for Enterprise Push
articles.summary: San Francisco-headquartered HR and enterprise software company Rippling is expanding its AI laboratory in Bengaluru, increasing hiring for senior engineering and leadership roles. India is Rippling’s largest office outside San Francisco, with over 2,000 employees, including 500+ engineers.

articles.headline: Google Unveils New AI Chips Targeting Regulated Enterprise Sectors
articles.summary: Alphabet's Google is rolling out new Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), TPU 8tx and 8i Max, custom-made AI chips. These chips are designed to enhance confidential computing and information access for AI agents, directly targeting regulated enterprise sectors.

articles.headline: Gold Drops Over 2% as US Inflation Fuels Fed Rate Hike Bets
articles.summary: Spot gold fell over 2% to $4,051.50/ounce as higher-than-expected US inflation data reinforced expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve stance. Futures also fell, while the dollar and Treasury yields rose, reducing gold's appeal.

articles.headline: NCLT Flags Fraud in HDIL Property Sale, Orders `2.38 Crore Recovery
articles.summary: The NCLT deemed a 2019 HDIL property sale by former promoters fraudulent and undervalued, citing discrepancies in sale consideration, lack of payment evidence, and document inconsistencies. It ordered the buyer and two former directors to jointly contribute `2.38 crore to HDIL's assets within 60 days.

articles.headline: Titan Sees Growth Driven by Studded Jewellery, Premium Watches, Engineering
articles.summary: Titan Company reported strong revenue and profit growth in Q2, fueled by studded jewellery (up 32%), premium watches, and its engineering business (TEAL). Lower-carat and lightweight jewellery are attracting value-conscious consumers. TEAL benefits from aerospace, electronics, and new-energy opportunities.

articles.headline: Cochin Shipyard Q2 Net Profit Drops 50% to `53.77 Crore
articles.summary: Cochin Shipyard Ltd reported a 50% decline in consolidated net profit to `53.77 crore for the September quarter, down from `107.52 crore a year ago. Total income rose to `1,331.81 crore, but total expenses also increased significantly.

articles.headline: Bajaj Finance Allots `5,800 Crore Warrants to Promoter Bajaj Finserv
articles.summary: NBFC Bajaj Finance allotted 5.74 crore warrants, worth `5,799.9 crore, to its promoter Bajaj Finserv on a preferential basis. Each warrant is convertible into an equity share, with a minimum of 25% consideration payable upon allotment.

articles.headline: National Framework Launched to Expedite Skilling Centre Approvals
articles.summary: The skill development ministry launched a national empanelment framework to streamline approvals for centres of excellence, including a green channel for established institutions. The move ensures only credible, outcome-oriented institutions receive government recognition, valid for three years.

articles.headline: Moody’s Forecasts Weaker Global Credit Conditions in 2027
articles.summary: Moody’s Ratings expects global credit conditions to weaken in 2027 due to higher financing costs, elevated energy prices, and political intervention. Major economies will expand, but sectors will face pressure, with AI-led transformation and security premiums driving risks and opportunities.

articles.headline: Iran War Fuels Inflation Surge Across G20 Economies
articles.summary: The Iran war has rapidly increased living costs globally, with Italy and France among the worst-hit G20 nations. India experienced the biggest inflation jump among G20 nations, but this was attributed to unusually low inflation prior to the conflict.

articles.headline: India-US Trade Talks Undeterred by Trump's Midterm Setback
articles.summary: India and the US continue negotiations on their bilateral trade agreement, with technical discussions on customs and trade facilitation ongoing. Officials state that President Donald Trump’s Republican Party losing majority in midterms will not impact trade pact talks.

articles.headline: Mobilising $1.3 Trillion Climate Finance by 2035 Requires System Overhaul
articles.summary: A COP30 report states mobilizing $1.3 trillion annually in climate finance for developing countries by 2035 is achievable but demands a fundamental overhaul of the global climate finance system. It proposes $882 billion from private, $351-384 billion from public, and $40-144 billion from carbon markets.

articles.headline: Limiting 1.5°C Overshoot, Electrification Top COP31 Priorities
articles.summary: Limiting global temperature overshoot of 1.5°C and accelerating electrification are key priorities at COP31. The Turkiye-Australia leadership seeks these issues in the conference's cover decision, emphasizing the need for deep emissions reductions and adaptation finance.

articles.headline: PHD Chamber Urges Abolition of LTCG, Halving STCG Tax
articles.summary: The PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry recommends abolishing long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on equity, halving short-term capital gains (STCG) tax to 10%, and lowering STT rates. It also proposes increasing basic customs duty to 20% on imported consumer durables and electronics to boost domestic manufacturing.

articles.headline: AI Drives Profound Transformation in Management Education
articles.summary: Management education is undergoing a profound transformation due to AI and data science. Business schools are integrating AI literacy, data-driven decision-making, and digital strategy into curricula, re-evaluating assessments, and training faculty to prepare students for an AI-augmented world.

articles.headline: Energy Security Needs Drive Surge in Hardware Startup Funding
articles.summary: Funding for energy infrastructure hardware startups is surging, driven by energy security needs rather than climate concerns. India's reliance on imported oil, gas, and battery components pushes investment towards domestic hardware to reduce import dependence and support renewable energy expansion.

articles.headline: Specialized Temperature Control Systems Present Opportunity for Electronics Makers
articles.summary: Specialized manufacturing of temperature control systems for AI data centers offers high-margin opportunities. Local production could challenge established hubs, with Dixon Technologies pursuing silicon-photonics and optical transceivers. Samsung, LG, Blue Star, and PG Electroplast are eyeing this growing segment.

articles.headline: India Focuses on Products with High Export Potential in South Asia
articles.summary: India is identifying products with strong export demand or potential in South Asian countries to boost trade. Issues like pesticide residues for turmeric/chilli in Sri Lanka and certification delays for yarn to Bangladesh are being addressed. India aims to scale exports to $1 billion in these markets.

articles.headline: Trump Hints at Diplomacy with Iran After Midterm Elections
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump signaled willingness to pursue diplomacy and wind down the Iran war after meeting Qatar's PM. This follows Republican midterm losses, with many blaming the conflict. Trump stated further strikes won't be necessary, and the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

articles.headline: Brent Crude Drops Below $90/bbl on Trump's Iran War Remarks
articles.summary: Brent crude futures fell below $90 per barrel for the first time since August 31, extending losses after President Trump hinted at diplomacy with Iran. Negotiations between Iran and the US are expected to continue, with economic pressure as the best way to resolve the conflict.

articles.headline: US Evacuates Aircraft from Second British Base After Iran Threat
articles.summary: The US military evacuated planes from RAF Mildenhall, a second British airbase, following a threat from Iran. Two refueling tankers were diverted to Germany, and others moved, weeks after bombers were withdrawn from another base due to suspected Iran-linked security threats.

articles.headline: Microsoft Overtakes Nvidia in Market Cap, Now World's Second Most Valuable
articles.summary: Microsoft surpassed Nvidia to become the world's second-most valuable company, as Nvidia's shares fell 6%. Nvidia shed over $470 billion in market value over two sessions amid concerns over CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of espionage.

articles.headline: Alleged Spy Alice Huang Facilitated $7.5 Billion Nvidia Chip Shipments to China
articles.summary: Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, allegedly a spy and linked to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, reportedly facilitated shipments of at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia's chips to Chinese firms. She used a network of companies to acquire and move banned H100, H200, and A100 chips into China.

articles.headline: US Consumer Prices Rise Slightly in October, Core Prices Stable
articles.summary: US inflation was higher than expected in October, with consumer prices rising 0.4% from September, down from 0.6% the previous month. Excluding food and energy, core prices rose 0.3%. The Labor Department did not report a yearly inflation rate due to a 2025 government shutdown.

articles.headline: China's Trade Surplus Exceeds $1 Trillion for Second Consecutive Year
articles.summary: China's trade surplus surpassed $1 trillion for a second consecutive year, with October exports surging 35.2% year-on-year. While exports grew rapidly, led by high-tech goods, the surplus narrowed slightly last month to $105.3 billion due to a recovery in imports, especially crude oil.

articles.headline: US First Nation to Fully Shun UN Human Rights Review Process
articles.summary: The United States is set to become the first country to fully shun the UN's universal periodic review of its human rights record since the Human Rights Council's creation two decades ago. The Trump administration previously pulled the US out of the council, citing anti-US/Israel bias.

articles.headline: California Voters Reject Measure to Tax Billionaires' Net Worth
articles.summary: California voters rejected Proposition 40, a first-in-the-nation measure to tax billionaires' net worth. The defeat is a win for Democratic leaders, including Governor Gavin Newsom, who opposed it, amidst concerns that such a tax would prompt ultra-wealthy taxpayers to leave the state.

articles.headline: BMW Adapts Luxury Pitch to Changing Indian Market and EV Opportunity
articles.summary: BMW Group India CEO Hardeep Singh Brar discusses adapting to the changing luxury car buyer, focusing on engineering, driving dynamics, and rear-seat comfort for the Indian market. EV sales grew 78% in H1, with long-wheelbase models now comprising 52% of their portfolio.

articles.headline: Instagram Tests 90-Minute Videos, Challenging YouTube for Long-Form Content
articles.summary: Instagram is testing 90-minute video formats in Brazil and the US, aiming to expand long-form content beyond short-form reels. This move positions Meta against YouTube and OTT platforms for advertising budgets and viewer time, especially as digital video consumption shifts to connected TVs.

articles.headline: GTA VI Release Expected to Spark Console Gaming Boom in India
articles.summary: Rockstar Games' GTA VI, launching on consoles on November 19, is expected to bring a significant console gaming boom in India. Industry players anticipate it will reignite gaming culture and boost PC and console sales, despite its `5,999+ price being higher than the average annual gaming spend.

articles.headline: Beauty Brands Focus on Packaging to Stand Out in Crowded Market
articles.summary: Beauty brands are increasingly using distinctive and innovative packaging as a core aspect of brand identity and consumer experience. Packaging is seen as a "silent brand ambassador" and a tool for on-screen visibility and cultural relevance, with brands also focusing on sustainability and design communication.

articles.headline: Agilitas Sports Aims to Build India's Own Sportswear Giant
articles.summary: Abhishek Ganguly, former Puma India CEO, founded Agilitas Sports to build an Indian sportswear company with its own manufacturing engine, brands (Lotto, One8), and retail network (SportsYard). The aim is to compete globally by controlling the value chain to quickly respond to consumer signals.

articles.headline: 7 Tech and Media Trends Reshaping Gen-Z Weddings in India
articles.summary: Gen-Z weddings in India are heavily tech-mediated, evolving with trends like AI for guest calls and mood boards, wedding content creators for instant vertical clips, QR codes for cash gifts, and face recognition apps for photo sharing. WhatsApp is now a central control room for planning.

articles.headline: Amazon Prime Adds Uber Eats, Escalating Food Delivery Wars
