articles.summary: Amazon is adding Uber Eats to its Prime membership benefits in the US, allowing members to order from hundreds of thousands of restaurants with no delivery fees over $25. This escalates competition in the food delivery market, following Amazon's Grubhub partnership and DoorDash's Instacart bid.

articles.headline: New Godzilla Film Tops US Box Office, Sets Record for Japanese Live-Action
articles.summary: 'Godzilla Minus Zero' became the highest-grossing movie in the US last weekend, generating $31.6 million and setting a record for a Japanese-language, live-action picture. Its predecessor won an Oscar for visual effects, showing a growing appetite for non-Hollywood films.

articles.headline: Crafting Ads to Be Remembered: Louis Vuitton's 'A Journey' as a Benchmark
articles.summary: Sagar Mahabaleshwarkar discusses Louis Vuitton's 'A Journey' ad campaign (2008) as a benchmark for crafting memorable advertisements. The film moves beyond product to personal journeys, using visuals, narration, music, and editing to evoke feeling rather than simply sell, serving the idea profoundly.

articles.headline: Private Indian Dairy Players Succeed Where MNCs Failed
articles.summary: Private Indian dairy companies like Milky Mist and Hatsun Agro Product are challenging cooperatives and succeeding where global MNCs struggled. Their growth is attributed to leveraging the cooperative movement, building closer farmer relationships, and focusing on high-margin value-added products over liquid milk.

articles.headline: Indian Marketers Increase Sponsorship Spend, AI Use Rises
articles.summary: Nielsen's Annual Marketing Report 2026 shows 94% of Indian marketers expect to increase sponsorship and event media spend. 98% now use AI. A Boston Consulting Group study found only 54% trust Black Friday discounts, with social media's inspiration share falling 9%.

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO admits affair with alleged Chinese spy amid security probe
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a woman suspected by US officials of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The scandal, involving potential export control violations by cloud firm Megaspeed, caused Nvidia's stock to drop 4%, erasing $200 billion in valuation. The board has launched an inquiry into whether national security or trade secrets were compromised.

articles.headline: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defends war moves amid impeachment threats
articles.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated he would stand by operations executed during the Iran war, despite moves to impeach him for alleged abuse of power. Speaking at a news conference, Hegseth expressed pride in the actions taken, signaling defiance against congressional critics as trilateral peace talks begin elsewhere.

articles.headline: Irdai Forms Working Groups to Develop Risk-Based Capital Framework
articles.summary: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai) has formed two working groups to align the proposed risk-based capital (RBC) regime with Indian Accounting Standards. The groups, comprising life and non-life insurance experts, have one month to prepare an exposure draft. The shift aims to link capital requirements directly to the risks carried by insurers.

articles.headline: Election Commission Extends Model Code Restrictions to Retired Officials
articles.summary: The Election Commission has ruled that Model Code of Conduct restrictions applicable to serving government employees will now also apply to retired officials engaged by the government. Ahead of polls in five states next year, the EC emphasized that such individuals must maintain political neutrality and refrain from participating in election campaigns or canvassing.

articles.headline: Medical devices PLI scheme extended to FY36 with relaxed rules
articles.summary: The Centre has extended the production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for domestic medical device manufacturing until 2035-36. The department of pharmaceuticals has also invited fresh applications under the revised rules. The extension is intended to provide long-term policy certainty and boost domestic production of critical healthcare equipment.

articles.headline: Urban Youth Unemployment Rises to Six-Quarter High of 18.9 Per Cent
articles.summary: Unemployment among India’s urban youth aged 15–29 rose to 18.9% in the July-September quarter, according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey. While urban youth unemployment increased, the combined national youth rate fell to 15.3% due to a decline in rural joblessness. Kerala recorded the highest overall unemployment rate at 8.7%, while Karnataka saw the lowest at 2.8%.

articles.headline: Blackstone to invest ₹5,000 crore for 16% stake in IIFL Finance
articles.summary: Blackstone will invest ₹5,000 crore in IIFL Finance through compulsorily convertible preference shares. The deal is part of a ₹6,414-crore capital raise to strengthen the NBFC's balance sheet and expand its gold loan business. The infusion is expected to raise IIFL's capital adequacy ratio to 30%, aiding expansion and potentially reducing future borrowing costs.

articles.headline: SoftBank reports $7 billion loss on US AI data centre writedowns
articles.summary: SoftBank Group Corp. posted a ¥1.12 trillion ($7.1 billion) net loss, its first in nearly two years. The loss was driven by a $3.7 billion writedown on US data centre projects and non-refundable advance payments for power generation. The results reflect growing investor fears regarding the long-term sustainability and costs associated with AI infrastructure growth.

articles.headline: Adani Group Plans $120 Billion Capital Expenditure Over Next Five Years
articles.summary: Executives at the Adani Group announced plans to invest more than $120 billion across its core infrastructure and energy platforms over the next five years. The investment will average over $20 billion annually, spanning sectors such as ports, airports, power, and renewables. The move underscores the conglomerate's aggressive expansion strategy in India's emerging growth platforms.

articles.headline: Anthropic targets $90 billion valuation in record-breaking IPO and placement
articles.summary: Claude chatbot maker Anthropic is seeking up to $64.4 billion in its IPO and a $26 billion private placement from firms like Nvidia, Google, and Microsoft. At the top price range, the company could be valued at $1 trillion. The filing revealed that 90% of Anthropic’s code is now written by AI, though operating expenses surged to $17.5 billion in the third quarter.

articles.headline: M John Harrison Wins Booker Prize for Science Fiction Novel
articles.summary: M John Harrison’s 'The End of Everything' has won the 2026 Booker Prize, making it the first bona fide science fiction novel to receive the award. At 81, Harrison is the oldest author to win the prize. The novel, which explores Britain being overrun by aliens, was praised by judges for its literary depth and its exploration of the failure of explanation in modern society.

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi Memoir Details Business Dissatisfaction with UPA 2 Government
articles.summary: In her autobiography 'Belonging: A Journey of Love,' Sonia Gandhi states that the business world backed the BJP in 2014 due to perceived 'policy paralysis' in the UPA 2 government. She credits Manmohan Singh's leadership for weathering the 2008 economic crisis and highlights the balance between economic growth and social justice maintained through the National Advisory Council.

articles.headline: MRF Reports 23 Per Cent Net Profit Drop Despite Higher Revenue
articles.summary: Tyre manufacturer MRF Ltd posted a 22.8% decline in consolidated net profit to ₹417.19 crore for the July-September quarter. The drop occurred despite a 17.4% rise in revenue from operations to ₹8,660.19 crore, as elevated raw material costs hit operating performance. The company saw double-digit sales growth across both original equipment and replacement segments.

articles.headline: Jaguar Land Rover to Launch First Electric Vehicles in India by 2027
articles.summary: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) plans to enter the Indian electric vehicle market in 2027 with models including the Range Rover Electric and Range Rover Sport Electric. The luxury automaker also plans to introduce the new Jaguar GT next year. JLR views India as a key growth market and believes the timing is appropriate for premium EV expansion.

articles.headline: India on Track to Achieve $1 Trillion Exports Target says Goyal
articles.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India is well on track to hit its $1 trillion exports target for the current financial year. Exports of goods and services reached $480 billion in the April-September period, covering 48% of the goal. Goyal urged the automobile industry to increase its focus on global markets to boost overall trade numbers.

articles.headline: Zomato Founder Deepinder Goyal's Temple Wearable Sparks Scientific Scrutiny
articles.summary: Deepinder Goyal's new wellness wearable, Temple, which claims to track brain blood flow and "entropy," faces backlash for its claims and `85,000 price. Doctors question its scientific validation, while the debate on social media has become a clash between loyalty and critical examination of expertise.
